([[Indianapolis, Indiana]]) | college = * [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]] (2019–2021) * [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 19 | draft_team = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team1 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[Memphis Hustle]] | years3 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team3 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team4 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2022) * Second-team All-[[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] (2021) * MVC All-Newcomer Team (2020) * MVC All-Freshman Team (2020) }} '''Jacob Glen LaRavia''' ({{IPAc-en|l|ə|ˈ|r|eɪ|v|iː|ə}} {{respell|lə|RAY|vee|ə}};[https://s3.grizzliesapp.com/assets/media_guides/MG_22-23_Media_Guide_FullBook.pdf Memphis Grizzlies 2022–23 Media Guide (scroll down to page 48).] Retrieved October 21, 2023. born November 3, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State Sycamores]] and the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]. After leading his high school team, [[Lawrence Central High School|Lawrence Central]], to its first sectional title since 2012, LaRavia played two seasons of college basketball at Indiana State. With the Sycamores, he was named to the [[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] All-Freshman and All-Newcomer teams as a freshman and was named to the Second-team All-MVC in his sophomore season. For his junior season, LaRavia transferred to Wake Forest and was named to the [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC Second Team]]. He was drafted 19th overall in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] before being traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. ==Early life== LaRavia is the son of Jeff and Becky LaRavia. His family moved from [[Pasadena, California]] to [[Indianapolis]] when LaRavia was five years old. LaRavia played basketball for [[Lawrence Central High School]] in Indianapolis, where he was teammates with [[Nijel Pack]] and [[Dre Davis]]. He had a limited role until his senior season, in which he became the team's leading scorer.{{cite web |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle |title=Jake LaRavia's breakout year a big reason No. 2 Lawrence Central has state title aspirations |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/07/siu-edwardsville-recruit-jake-laravia-leads-way-lawrence-central/3090800002/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=March 7, 2019}} As a senior, LaRavia averaged 17.3 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.3 steals per game, earning Indiana All-Star honors. He helped Lawrence Central win its first sectional title since 2012. LaRavia first committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball|SIU Edwardsville]] but reopened his recruitment after a coaching change. He later committed to [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]].{{cite web |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle |title=Lawrence Central's Jake LaRavia commits to Indiana State |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/04/14/basketball-recruiting-jake-laravia-commits-indiana-state-sycamores/3465001002/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=April 14, 2019}} ==College career== As a freshman at Indiana State, LaRavia averaged 9.4 points and 5.9 rebounds per game. He was named to the All-Newcomer and All-Freshman Teams in the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC).{{cite web |title=Key and LaRavia Named Preseason All-Missouri Valley Conference; Sycamores Picked Fourth in MVC Preseason Poll |url=https://gosycamores.com/news/2020/10/14/basketball-key-and-laravia-named-preseason-all-missouri-valley-conference-sycamores-picked-fourth-in-mvc-preseason-poll |publisher=Indiana State University Athletics |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=October 15, 2020}} In his sophomore season, LaRavia averaged 12.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game, earning second-team All-MVC recognition. Following the departure of coach [[Greg Lansing]], he transferred to [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite web |last=Gordon |first=Todd Aaron |title=LaRavia era at ISU is over as forward commits to Wake Forest |url=https://www.tribstar.com/laravia-era-at-isu-is-over-as-forward-commits-to-wake-forest/article_d0d95e1d-ade6-5fe9-8a33-23bd2d0c0122.html |website=[[Tribune-Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=March 16, 2021}} On January 22, 2022, LaRavia recorded a career-high 31 points, 10 rebounds and four assists in a 98–76 win against [[2021–22 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]].{{cite web |title=Jake LaRavia scores 31 as Wake Forest beats North Carolina 98-76 |url=https://www.wfmynews2.com/article/sports/jake-laravia-scores-31-as-wake-forest-beats-north-carolina-98-76/83-ff81c76d-6359-4be8-8a24-fccb260dc1df |publisher=[[WFMY-TV]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=January 23, 2022}} He averaged 14.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game as a junior. He was named to the [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference Second Team]].{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |title=Wake Forest junior Jake LaRavia invited to NBA draft combine |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/05/04/wake-forest-jake-laravia-nba-draft-combine/ |publisher=The Rookie Wire |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=May 4, 2022}} On March 29, 2022, LaRavia declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Geisinger |first=Brian |title=All-ACC F Jake LaRavia declares for Draft, will maintain eligibility |url=https://accsports.com/teams/wake-forest/all-acc-f-jake-laravia-declares-for-draft-will-maintain-eligibility/ |publisher=ACCSports.com |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=March 30, 2022}} On June 1, 2022, he announced that he would remain in the draft and forgo his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |title=Potential first-round pick Jake LaRavia to remain in NBA draft |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/06/01/wake-forest-jake-laravia-nba-draft-agent/ |publisher=The Rookie Wire |access-date=June 12, 2022 |date=June 1, 2022}} ==Professional career== === Memphis Grizzlies (2022–2025) === LaRavia was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 19th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. His draft rights were later traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], along with a future second-round pick, in exchange for the 22nd and 29th picks in the draft, which would later become [[Walker Kessler]] and [[TyTy Washington]].{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2022 |title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire draft rights to Jake LaRavia and future second round pick from Minnesota Timberwolves |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-draft-rights-to-jake-laravia-and-future-second-round-pick-from-minnesota-timberwolves-220624 |access-date=July 28, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} LaRavia joined the Grizzlies' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612763/grizzlies |access-date=July 28, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} In his Summer League debut, he scored thirteen points in a 103–99 win over the [[2022–23 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |date=July 5, 2022 |title=Memphis Grizzlies vs Philadelphia 76ers Jul 5, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/mem-vs-phi-1622200001/box-score#box-score |access-date=July 28, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On October 19, 2022, LaRavia made his NBA debut, recording five points and two rebounds in a 115–112 overtime win over the [[2022–23 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]].{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Clay |date=October 19, 2022 |title=Morant's 34 points lead Grizzlies to OT win over Knicks |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200009 |access-date=March 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He was assigned to the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]] on March 23, 2023.{{Cite web |date=March 23, 2023 |title=Grizzlies' Jake LaRavia: Headed to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-jake-laravia-headed-to-g-league/amp/ |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com}} === Sacramento Kings (2025) === On February 6, 2025, LaRavia was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Washington Wizards]] in which Washington acquired [[Marcus Smart]], [[Alex Len]], [[Colby Jones]], and one first-round pick while the Grizzlies received [[Marvin Bagley III]], [[Johnny Davis (basketball, born 2002)|Johnny Davis]], and two second-round picks.{{Cite web |title=Wizards add Marcus Smart in multi-team deal with Grizzlies, Kings |url=https://www.nba.com/news/wizards-grizzlies-kings-smart-laravia-len-trade?m= Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-forward-jake-laravia|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Forward Jake LaRavia|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2025}}{{cite web | access-date=2025-12-06}} LaRavia appeared in all 82 games (including 43 starts) for Los Angeles during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 8.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, and
